### 1.  A basic consequence

Put  

\[
P(n):\qquad f\bigl(f(n)+n\bigr)=2f(n) .
\]

If we denote \(a=n_{0}=n,\;a_{1}=f(n)+n\) and write \(a_{k+1}=a_{k}+f(a_{k})\)
we obtain inductively  

\[
\boxed{\;f\bigl(n+(2^{k}-1)f(n)\bigr)=2^{k}f(n)\qquad(k=0,1,2,\ldots )\;}\tag{1}
\]

Indeed (1) is true for \(k=0\); if it holds for a fixed \(k\) then, using
\(P\bigl(n+(2^{k}-1)f(n)\bigr)\),

\[
f\!\Bigl(\underbrace{n+(2^{k}-1)f(n)}_{=a_{k}}
      +f\bigl(a_{k}\bigr)\Bigr)
   =2f\bigl(a_{k}\bigr)
   =2\cdot2^{k}f(n)=2^{k+1}f(n),
\]

which is (1) for \(k+1\).

Hence from any integer \(n\) we obtain an infinite increasing sequence  

\[
n_{k}=n+(2^{k}-1)f(n)
\qquad(k=0,1,2,\ldots )
\]

and
\(f(n_{k})=2^{k}f(n)\).
The mapping  

\[
T(x)=x+f(x)

has the property that \(f(T^{k}(x))=2^{k}f(x)\); consequently a number can be
written in the form  

\[
\tag{2} n=r+(2^{k}-1)a\qquad (k\ge 0)
\]

where \(a=f(r)\) and \(1\le r\le a\).  
The integer \(r\) is the **root** of the element \(n\) and it is the unique

\[
